verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The problem is stated, and message #3 measures a statement-lifespan leak of about 104 MiB for 50k rows through views and partitioned tables. The fix is confined to trigger.c and adds no user-visible surface. Confidence is medium because the safety of the added free depends on code that was not read.

brief.title: Free leaked tuple in BEFORE/INSTEAD OF row triggers
brief.problem: ExecBRInsertTriggers, ExecBRUpdateTriggers, ExecIRInsertTriggers and ExecIRUpdateTriggers leak a copied HeapTuple when the slot is virtual and the trigger returns NEW unchanged (or NULL in ExecIRUpdateTriggers). Users hit it with triggers on views and with BEFORE INSERT triggers on partitioned tables routing to same-layout partitions. Memory grows per row for the whole statement.
brief.proposed_design: The patch frees the tuple fetched from the virtual slot when the trigger hands back the same tuple. The change is confined to src/backend/commands/trigger.c and is meant for back-patching to 14.
author_claims: The leak exists on master and goes back to v14 at least.
A reviewer measured ExecutorState at about 104 MiB on master for 50k rows with a 1 kB column, flat with v1.
The partitioned-table case drops from about 105 MiB to about 544 KiB with the patch, per a reviewer.
Assigning to NEW in PL/pgSQL, even NEW.id := NEW.id, avoids the leak on master.
brief.thread_state: Chao Li and Surya Poondla reviewed and approved; v2 fixed a commit message typo and added the partitioned-table case. No committer has replied, and nothing is open.
unclear: The material does not say whether the patch adds a regression test or how one could check for the leak.
The thread does not say whether the fix applies cleanly to all branches back to 14.
The thread does not say whether other trigger paths, such as delete triggers or foreign tables, have the same leak.

questions: Can a C trigger function keep or return a pointer into the tuple that the patch now frees, and if so, what guards against use after free?
Does the patch apply to every branch back to 14, or do some branches need a different version?
Do other trigger paths, such as delete triggers or triggers on foreign tables, leak the same copied tuple?
Does the patch add a regression test, and if not, how would a later change that brings the leak back be noticed?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows executor tuple slots and trigger.c tuple ownership would have to own it. No committer has replied in the visible thread; the commit message credits Andres Freund only as reporter.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the added free being safe in six supported branches, including for C trigger functions in extensions. A mistake there is a use after free in released minor versions.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 within days, fixing the commit message and adding the partitioned-table case from message #3.

priority.reason: The leak reaches users of INSTEAD OF triggers on views and BEFORE INSERT triggers on partitioned tables, at about 104 MiB per 50k rows in message #3. The patch is about 3 KiB in one file, with two reviewers approving.

provisional_note: Without the code, it could not be checked that the freed tuple is never referenced afterwards, or that the free happens only when the slot made a copy. The four functions named in the commit message were not compared with other trigger paths.

precedents_retrieved.title: Leaking memory in text_overlay function
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds explicit pfree calls to text_overlay in varlena.c to free the two substrings from text_substring and one intermediate concatenation result. The author argued that built-in functions should free the memory they allocate.
precedents_retrieved.objection: SQL-called functions run in short-lived memory contexts that are reset at the end of each tuple cycle, so not freeing memory in them is intentional. Adding retail pfree calls everywhere would make the system slower than a MemoryContextReset, and the patch showed no query-lifespan leak. The author accepted this and closed the thread.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There are places where it's important to avoid leaking memory, certainly.
But I don't think this is one of them, unless you can demonstrate a
scenario with query-lifespan or worse leakage.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade: fix memory leak in SLRU I/O code
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes FreeSlruWrite() in pg_upgrade's slru_io.c free state->dir and state->fn as well as the SlruSegState struct, through a new FreeSlruSegState() cleanup helper. It also switches the allocation of state->dir from pstrdup() to pg_strdup() to follow frontend conventions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier saw nothing worth changing, because SlruSegState is allocated once, state->fn is already freed when switching segments, and the memory goes away when pg_upgrade exits. The author agreed the leak was not a real problem, said he was happy to drop the patch, and withdrew it. Álvaro Herrera suggested replacing pg_free(state) with a comment instead.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: In short, I see nothing worth changing.

precedents_retrieved.title: Re: BUG #18741: Detaching a partition referencing a partitioned table fails with a trigger-related error
precedents_retrieved.summary: Alexander Lakhin reported that detaching a partition fails with an internal trigger error when the partition has a foreign key to a partitioned table and its new parent has no matching foreign key. Tender Wang and jian he discussed fixing this, mainly by rejecting such ATTACH PARTITION commands except where the partition references a non-partitioned table or its own parent's hierarchy.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. They contain the bug report and two design suggestions with no patch, review or decision, and they do not say why the entry was withdrawn.

precedents_retrieved.title: BUG Segfault triggered by reentrancy in ri_triggers.c
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a segfault from a use-after-free in RI_FKey_cascade_del, which occurs when the plancache is reset while a reentrant RI trigger runs on a self-referential table whose BEFORE DELETE triggers delete rows from the same table. It adds a test that reproduces the crash and reentrancy guards that reference-count RI plans in execution so they are not freed while active.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Álvaro Herrera confirmed the crash and did not reject a fix, but he called deleting other rows from BEFORE DELETE triggers wrong usage and asked whether AFTER DELETE triggers would avoid the problem. The entry was withdrawn the same day, with no visible reply from the author.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
However, while I'm not saying that we absolutely shouldn't fix this, I
think it's wrong usage to have BEFORE DELETE triggers delete other rows.

precedents_retrieved.title: Row Level Security, leakproof-ness, and performance implications
precedents_retrieved.summary: The thread started from slow queries under row-level security, caused by many built-in operator functions not being marked leakproof, and a patch marked enum_eq, enum_ne, textin and textout leakproof. Later proposals were a documentation patch listing RLS restrictions on the CREATE POLICY page, and Joe Conway's idea to redact error messages sent to clients plus a GUC to treat all functions as leakproof.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut wrote that redacting error messages had been found not to satisfy the leakproofness criteria, and Joe Conway accepted that the consensus was against him. Robert Haas suggested doing it outside core, with a logging hook and functions marked leakproof by hand, and doubted that customers could be supported with redacted messages. Peter also found the CREATE POLICY page the wrong place for the documentation patch and asked how a list of non-leakproof operators would be kept complete. The visible messages do not show which of these two patches this entry is.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think that approach has been found not to actually satisfy the leakproofness criteria.

precedents_retrieved.title: Change tuple table slot for Unique node to "virtual"
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Heikki Linnakangas, David Rowley, Ashutosh Bapat
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changed the Unique node's result slot from a minimal tuple slot to a virtual slot, because the copy into a minimal tuple slot (with palloc) made DISTINCT slower than the equivalent GROUP BY. A later version used the outer child's slot type instead of a fixed type.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Benchmarks showed mixed results. Heikki Linnakangas found a slowdown when the input is a minimal tuple from a Sort, and David Rowley measured Q2 and Q3 as slower with the revised patch because tts_virtual_materialize() costs more. Ashutosh Bapat doubted the change was worth pursuing when only one query improved clearly. The author then asked how slot types should be chosen across all materialization nodes, and the entry was withdrawn after an offline discussion.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Q1 is consistently giving performance > 25% for both of us. But other queries aren't showing a whole lot improvement.

precedents_retrieved.title: Code comments: why some text-handling functions are leakproof
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a code comment on bttextcmp() that explains why some text-processing functions are marked leakproof and others are not. The text is close to a verbatim copy of an earlier mailing-list explanation by Tom Lane.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas said a developer changing leakproof markings would not likely find a comment on bttextcmp() or in the optimizer README, and that not everyone agrees with the stated rationale. Tom Lane agreed on placement and suggested a new <sect1> in xfunc.sgml next to the section on volatility categories. Greg Stark returned the entry with feedback and asked for a new patch that moves the text to xfunc.sgml.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It doesn't seem particularly likely that someone who is thinking about
changing this in the future would notice the comment in the place
where you propose to put it, nor that they would read the optimizer
README.

precedents_retrieved.title: BUG Segfault triggered by reentrancy in ri_triggers.c
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a crash in RI_FKey_cascade_del: on a self-referential table whose BEFORE DELETE triggers delete rows from the same table, a plan cache reset during a reentrant RI trigger frees a plan that is still running. It adds reference counts to ri_triggers.c so that plans in execution are not freed, plus a regression test that reproduces the crash.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Álvaro Herrera confirmed the crash and did not reject a fix, but he argued that BEFORE DELETE triggers should not delete other rows and asked whether AFTER DELETE triggers would avoid it. The author posted a new version that fixes failing regression tests, and the entry was withdrawn the same day without explanation.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit e21cbb4, as the switch to EVP routines requires a
more careful design where we would need to have at least our wrapper
routines return a status instead of issuing an error by themselves to
let the caller do the error handling.  The memory handling was also
incorrect and could cause leaks in the backend if a failure happened,
requiring most likely a callback to do the necessary cleanup as the only
clean way to be able to allocate an EVP context requires the use of an
allocation within OpenSSL.  The potential rework of the wrappers also
impacts the fallback implementation when not building with OpenSSL.

Originally, prairiedog has reported a compilation failure, but after
discussion with Tom Lane this needs a better design.

This reverts the following commits:
1b5617eb844cd2470a334c1d2eec66cf9b39c41a Describe (auto-)analyze behavior for partitioned tables
0e69f705cc1a3df273b38c9883fb5765991e04fe Set pg_class.reltuples for partitioned tables

There are efficiency issues in this code when handling databases with
large numbers of partitions, and it doesn't look like there isn't any
trivial way to handle those.  There are some other issues as well.  It's
now too late in the cycle for nontrivial fixes, so we'll have to let
Postgres 14 users continue to manually deal with ANALYZE their
partitioned tables, and hopefully we can fix the issues for Postgres 15.

I kept [most of] be280cdad298 ("Don't reset relhasindex for partitioned
tables on ANALYZE") because while we added it due to 0827e8af70f4, it is
a good bugfix in its own right, since it affects manual analyze as well
as autovacuum-induced analyze, and there's no reason to revert it.

I retained the addition of relkind 'p' to tables included by
pg_stat_user_tables, because reverting that would require a catversion
bump.
Also, in pg14 only, I keep a struct member that was added to
PgStat_TabStatEntry to avoid breaking compatibility with existing stat
files.

Backpatch to 14.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P1] was rejected because it showed no query-lifespan leak, while message #3 here measures ExecutorState growth of about 104 MiB over one statement, so that reason does not apply. Message #1 says Andres reported the leak while reviewing FOR PORTION OF and does not report any earlier rejected attempt at this fix.

The patch adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object or psql change, and it does not change query results or what pg_dump emits. Back-patching to 14 changes only memory use. [P1] does not apply, because message #3 shows a statement-lifespan leak of about 100 MiB per 50k rows. Whether freeing the tuple is safe for C trigger functions that keep the returned pointer is a safety question for another angle.

The patch only frees a backend-local HeapTuple in trigger.c. It touches no on-disk format, WAL, catalog, wire protocol or replication state. A back-patch could break ABI only if it changed exported signatures or structs, and the brief describes a change inside function bodies. Whether ownership of the returned tuple stays correct for callers and extensions cannot be checked without the code.

The patch adds no privilege, no new surface and no new exposure. It frees a per-row copy that today grows for the whole statement, so it reduces memory use that an ordinary user can trigger. Whether the freed tuple could still be referenced is a safety question that needs the code to answer, and it is outside the security angle. [P1] does not apply, because message #3 shows a statement-lifespan leak.

From the maintenance and fit angle there is nothing to send. This is a back-patchable bugfix confined to trigger.c, with no new API, GUC, catalog or per-row cost for non-users. [P1] does not apply, because its reason required a query-lifespan leak and message #3 shows one of about 104 MiB per statement. Whether other paths need the same free, such as FOR PORTION OF or delete and foreign-table triggers, and whether a per-tuple memory context would be the more durable fix, are review questions. Neither carries a concrete failure scenario against this patch.

This is a bug fix for a statement-lifetime leak in ExecutorState, which nothing in Postgres or in an extension can replace. The PL/pgSQL workaround of assigning to NEW is a user-side trick, so it does not meet the need. [P1] does not apply because its reason was per-tuple context reset, and message #3 shows query-lifespan growth.

This is a bug fix for a statement-lifespan memory leak, so the demand test does not apply in the usual way. Message #3 shows about 104 MiB of ExecutorState growth for 50k rows through common paths: INSTEAD OF triggers on views, and BEFORE INSERT triggers on partitioned tables. Users cannot opt out of this cost. [P1] does not fit, because its recorded reason was the lack of a query-lifespan leak, and this thread shows one.
